dev_notes: src/commands/redraft.mjs. Archived releases keep their place in releases.json with status "archived" and an "archive" path, which keeps versions 1..N contiguous; predecessorOf() returns null across the boundary, so every diff treats the first edition after a redraft as a first edition, and redraftReplaces() is what the renderers read for the note: the archived group, or for a release marked redraft: true by hand, every edition back to the previous redraft. predecessorOf() also returns null for a hand-marked redraft, so it prints as an inventory with no notes or summary; labelOf() does not advance on one unless it is the first release, and fileLabel() adds _redraft, so Version 3 is followed by Version 3 (redraft) and then Version 4. Set on the first release, the note says the list replaces reports sent some other way. The archive holds an archived.json marker: Project resolves the root three levels up and refuses every save. `redraft start` refuses a dirty .ledger/ and an open release with work on it (--force for both). The live corpus keeps config (areas reset), brand, STYLE.md and theme.css; compositions.json starts empty. bootstrap's redraft step stops before the cut, and `ledger redraft` on its own says what is left to do. The old-to-new pairing is same id, else Jaccard over name and description words, with a 0.12 threshold.

history.name: Redrafting the ledger
history.description: The command ledger redraft start sets the corpus aside in .ledger/archive/ and opens the next version on an empty one, for a fresh survey; version numbers and printed editions carry on. ledger redraft check has a coding agent put back anything the survey missed and write a note for the client, and ledger cut waits for it. The first edition after a redraft says the ledger is reorganized, and marks nothing as new.
